name: 15th Five-Year Plan
summary: Elevated AI to primary national objective; ~90% AI diffusion across economy by 2030 (~70% by 2027); advanced manufacturing + AI infra central priorities

name: Nationwide AI Data Center Buildout Plan
summary: Fund a nationwide network of interconnected data centers; >=80% of technology mandated domestic

name: AI & Robotics State Fund
summary: UPDATE to existing row: confirmed as NDRC-run state venture capital guidance fund targeting AI, robotics, quantum, hydrogen storage; expected to attract ~¥1tn (~$138bn) from local governments + private sector over 20 years. Explicit goals: accelerate humanoid robotics, smart manufacturing, AI integration.

name: Robotics & High-Tech Investment
summary: UPDATE to existing row: tied to 14th FYP Robot Industry Development Plan / 2035 Vision Outline; context — China's global share of industrial robot installations rose from ~1/5 to >1/2 of world demand over the past decade (2024: 295k units installed, 54% of global total).

name: 50% Domestic Equipment Mandate
summary: UPDATE to existing row: confirmed as an informal/unpublished directive — fab-expansion approval applications are reportedly rejected if domestic-equipment spend is below 50%; case-by-case flexibility granted for advanced production lines where domestic tools are not yet adequate; officials describe 50% as a floor, with long-term goal of exclusive domestic sourcing.

name: Indigenous EUV Program
summary: UPDATE to existing row: 2028 target should be read as a lab/prototype milestone (LDP source ~100-150W measured mid-2025, needs >250W for HVM; parallel SSMB synchrotron effort targets >1kW theoretical at Xiong'an facility) — not a volume-manufacturing parity date.

name: Equity Market Policy Pivot / 'Slow Bull'
summary: Policy shift treating equity market as strategic; support IPOs of less-sensitive AI champions; 'slow bull' management; buybacks/governance tools

name: National IC Industry Investment Fund ('Big Fund')
summary: UPDATE to existing row: Phase III size confirmed at RMB344bn (~$47.5bn), the largest of the three phases (Phase I $21.8bn 2014; Phase II $29.08bn 2019). Mandate explicitly includes HBM and AI-semiconductor value chain alongside manufacturing/equipment/materials; no public breakdown of memory-specific allocation identified.

name: US EDA Export Restriction on China
summary: BIS ordered Synopsys, Cadence and Siemens EDA to suspend software/technical support to Chinese customers in May-2025; later required case-by-case export licenses for all EDA sales to China. Catalyzed consolidation/investment in domestic EDA (Empyrean, Primarius).

name: Entity List Additions (Mar-2025 tranche)
summary: 42 PRC entities added to BIS Entity List, including Shenzhen Naura Microelectronics Equipment Co. and SMIC Advanced Technology R&D (Shanghai) Corporation, among 80 total entities across several countries.

name: MATCH Act (H.R.8170)
summary: Proposed US legislation to require allied-nation coordination on export controls; would ban ASML DUV shipments to China (~20% of ASML 2026 revenue) and references Hua Hong, SMIC, NAURA, AMEC, ACM Research explicitly. Not yet enacted.

name: DoD Section 1260H "Chinese Military Company" Listing (CXMT)
summary: CXMT designated a "Chinese military company" under NDAA Section 1260H; bars US government procurement/use of CXMT semiconductor products/services effective 23-Dec-2027. Distinct from (and precedes) any Commerce Entity List action, which remains under inter-agency consideration as of mid-2026, reportedly delayed for diplomatic reasons.

name: Commerce Entity List Addition (YMTC)
horizon: ongoing; YMTC litigating in federal court
summary: YMTC added to Commerce Department Entity List Dec-2022 as part of a 36-entity tranche; remains listed and subject to export-license requirements as of mid-2026. YMTC's status on the separate Pentagon 1260H list has fluctuated within 2026 (apparently removed Feb-2026, reinstated Jun-2026) — treat as unresolved/monitor.

name: MATCH Act (H.R.8170) — memory-sector application
summary: UPDATE/cross-reference to Pod 1's match-act-2026 row: the same proposed legislation would designate all CXMT chipmaking facilities as "covered facilities," applying Entity-List-equivalent export, servicing and technical-support restrictions specifically to CXMT (in addition to its L1/L2 equipment-sector provisions).

name: National AI Computing Grid Plan
currency_note: draft plan; RMB-denominated original not confirmed in reviewed sources
summary: Draft national plan for an AI computing grid run on 80% domestic chips; China Mobile/China Telecom to operate bulk of facilities; structurally excludes Nvidia/AMD from state-funded buildout

name: State-funded Data Center Domestic Chip Mandate
summary: Aug 2025: state-funded DCs required to source ≥50% chips domestically. Nov 2025: escalated to full ban on foreign accelerators in state-funded projects, including retrofit removal from <30%-complete builds. May 2026: 9 categories of domestic AI chips (Huawei, Alibaba, Biren, Moore Threads) cleared security review for gov/security-sensitive deployment

name: H200 Conditional Export Policy
summary: H200 sales to China approved conditionally: 25% export tax, capped at ≤50% of total H200 units sold to US customers, BIS case-by-case license review; excludes current Blackwell/upcoming Rubin GPUs; by 2026-05, 10 China firms cleared for H200 purchase

name: Entity List Additions — Chinese AI Chip Firms
summary: 13 Chinese entities added to US Entity List for advanced computing chip development, including Biren (multiple subsidiaries) and Moore Threads (multiple subsidiaries); bars access to advanced US foundries/EDA

name: National AI Data-Center Grid (NDRC)
summary: NDRC draft plan to connect thousands of data centers into a unified national computing grid; mandates ≥80% domestic-sourced technology incl. AI accelerators (favoring Huawei et al.), squeezing out Nvidia/AMD; state operators (China Mobile, China Telecom) to run bulk of DCs; builds on earlier "East Data West Compute" spatial initiative

name: "AI Plus" Initiative diffusion targets
summary: Targets next-gen intelligent application/agent adoption >70% by 2027, ~90% by 2030, "ubiquitous" by 2035; sector plans (AI Plus Manufacturing) and SOE pilot cohorts (Baosteel, XCMG, Haier — 15 "pioneer" smart factories, >70% AI-scenario coverage, 6,000+ deployed AI models) operationalize the targets; treated by analysts as directional signaling rather than hard KPIs

name: Humanoid Robot & Embodied Intelligence Standardization Program
summary: New policy: MIIT established dedicated Humanoid Robot and Embodied Intelligence Standardization Technical Committee (Dec-2025); released first national standard system covering the humanoid robot industry's full lifecycle (Mar-2026). China is leading IEC global standard formulation for elder-care robots and shaping international norms for robot safety/interoperability/data governance — a moat-by-standardization strategy.

name: Special Action Plan for Green and Low-Carbon Development of Data Centers
summary: New policy: targets average PUE ≤1.25 for new/upgraded large data centers (vs. national avg ~1.48 in 2023); mandates ≥80% renewable electricity sourcing for all new data centers as of 2025 (raised from a lower/optional threshold), with national computing-hub-region facilities also targeted for 80% renewable share by 2030.

name: 15th Five-Year Plan Nuclear Capacity Target
summary: New policy: 15th FYP targets 110GWe nuclear capacity by 2030 (from ~63GW operating in 2026), with a longer-term goal of 200GW by 2035. 36 reactor units under construction as of 2026 — half of global under-construction nuclear capacity.

name: East-Data-West-Compute (东数西算)
summary: UPDATE/new detail: 8 national computing hub nodes (5 western: Ningxia, Inner Mongolia, Gansu, Chengdu-Chongqing, Guizhou; 3 eastern: Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei, Yangtze River Delta, Greater Bay Area). As of 2026: 63% hub occupancy, 20ms inter-hub latency, >50,000 petaflops cluster compute at some western hubs (Qingyang, Zhongwei). Rationale: route AI-DC demand to curtailed/cheap western renewable power.

name: State Grid 15th FYP Capex Plan
summary: New policy: State Grid capex commitment of CNY4tn (+40% vs 14th FYP), funding 15 new UHV transmission lines (2026-2030) adding ~200GWh/yr renewable-connection capacity and +30-35% cross-provincial transmission capacity vs 2025 levels.

name: National IC Industry Investment Fund Phase I
summary: First phase of the Big Fund; backed early fab/equipment/memory investment

name: National IC Industry Investment Fund Phase II
summary: Second phase; broadened scope across equipment, materials, memory

name: National IC Industry Investment Fund Phase III
summary: Third phase, largest to date; six state banks contributed RMB114bn (33.14% stake)

name: Artificial Intelligence+ Initiative
summary: State Council Opinion [2025] No.11; targets >70% penetration of new-gen smart terminals/agents by 2027, >90% by 2030, full 'intelligent economy' by 2035

name: SOE AI-Adoption Mandate
summary: Mandated AI integration across state-owned enterprises; ~70% AI penetration target across key industrial sectors by 2027

name: Provincial/Municipal Computing-Power Vouchers
summary: Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen, Henan, Shandong, Chengdu, Ningbo issue vouchers covering up to 80% of AI compute-rental costs for SMEs, plus data/LLM-training subsidies

name: STAR Market Fifth Listing Standard Extension
summary: Extends pre-profit IPO access to large-model developers and quantum-tech firms; requires ~$591m market cap and government approval of core technology

name: HBM & FDPR/SME Export Control Expansion
summary: US BIS: first-ever country-wide HBM controls (>2GB/mm2 density); new Footnote-5 and SME Foreign Direct Product Rules extending US jurisdiction to non-US-made SME destined for China; ~140 entities added

name: H200/MI325X Case-by-Case Export Review
summary: US BIS shifts H200/MI325X China export license review from presumption-of-denial to case-by-case, 25% tariff, subject to security conditions

name: Rare-Earth/Gallium/Germanium Export-Control Suspension
summary: China suspends (not repeals) export controls on rare earths, gallium, germanium, antimony, superhard materials toward the US as part of the Busan trade truce

name: US Outbound Investment Security Program
summary: Treasury final rule restricting/screening US investment into Chinese AI, semiconductor, and quantum entities; broadened by Dec-2025 NDAA/COINS Act to add sectors (HPC, supercomputing, hypersonics) and countries
